---
title: "Activity A data dictionary"
---

## Origin and scope

These values are constructed teaching data. They are not measurements from a
real site. Each row is one reported ion in one near-neutral sample. Three sample
identities have six rows each. Samples A and C are designed to share the same
correct composition, but C includes a known decimal transcription error.
The identifiers A, B, and C are local to this activity and do not identify the
separate carbonate-unit example waters. The six ions form the complete major-ion set for this approximation; tiny H⁺
and OH⁻ terms and other species are omitted. No pH or metal speciation can be
inferred from these six totals alone.

## Original ion table

| Column | Meaning | Units or allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sample_id` | Constructed sample identifier | A, B, C |
| `ion` | Reported ionic species | Ca, Mg, Na, HCO3, Cl, SO4 |
| `concentration_mg_l` | Mass of the named ion per water volume | mg/L; HCO3 and SO4 are compound mass, not elemental C or S |
| `molar_mass_g_mol` | Supplied rounded molar mass of the named ion | g/mol; numerical value also mg/mmol |
| `charge` | Signed charge number | +2, +1, −1, or −2, as appropriate |

`sample_id` plus `ion` uniquely identifies a row. Zero would denote a specified
zero, while an unknown measurement would be `NA`; the supplied table has no
missing values. Never replace unknowns with zero merely to complete a balance.

## Correction record

`corrections.csv` gives sample and ion, the original and corrected concentrations
in mg/L, and a text evidence statement. The authoritative **constructed** lab
record gives C sulfate as 19.212 mg/L rather than 1.9212. The record is additional
information, not a value inferred solely from charge closure. Preserve the raw
CSV and create a corrected in-memory copy.

## Derived quantities

Divide the mass concentration by the numerical molar mass to obtain mmol/L.
Multiply by positive charge or negative charge magnitude to obtain positive or
negative meq/L contributions. Sum each charge sign within sample. The signed
imbalance is `100 * (cations - anions) / (cations + anions)` in percent.
A and B are distinct constructed compositions; they are not replicate treatments.
